question: For Cyanide, Total Recoverable and Total Dissolved Solids at Outfall 001, do the 'Report' entries in all effluent limitation columns (lbs/day and mg/l; monthly average and daily maximum) establish that no enforceable numeric discharge limit applies, such that numeric compliance comparison is not applicable?
source_locator: aztec/final_permit.pdf page 3 section part_i (Cyanide, Total Recoverable and Total Dissolved Solids rows in DISCHARGE LIMITATIONS table)
semantic_arguments: Column headers distinguishing effluent limitation units and averaging periods (lbs/day unless noted; mg/l unless noted; MONTHLY AVG; DAILY MAX) from monitoring requirement columns (MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY; SAMPLE TYPE)
Contrast on the same table with pollutants bearing explicit numeric maximum limits (e.g., Total Suspended Solids monthly average 20 mg/l and daily maximum 30 mg/l)
Use of 'Report' in all four limitation cells for both parameters versus numeric or 'N/A' entries for other pollutants
Section context: 'FINAL Effluent Limits – Outfall 001 – Intermittent Flow' under PART I limitations and monitoring requirements
Footnote *1 ('When discharging') attached to the quarterly monitoring frequency for these parameters
notes: Purpose A requires distinguishing enforceable numeric limits from report-only monitoring. The target rows contain only 'Report' in limitation columns while other parameters on the same outfall carry numeric maxima; resolving whether 'Report' denotes absence of a numeric effluent limit changes whether exceedance comparison is in scope.
